newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi court orders opposition leader to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Malawi court orders opposition leader to parliament.

text.p: Malawi's parliamentary opposition leader said on Tuesday authorities would have to put him in chains to force him to end his boycott and return to parliament.
National radio said Malawi's High Court had ruled that Gwanda Chakuamba must return immediately to parliament.

Chakuamba, vice-president of the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP), told Reuters he would not return to parliament because the High Court had not served him with the order although he had heard the radio broadcast.
"I'm not going. I can only go there in chains. But even in chains, I'm not going," he said.

The court ruling on Monday said a voter from Chakuamba's constituency had applied for the order because Chakuamba had not given good reasons for refusing to attend parliment and was denying his constituents full parliamentary representation.
Chakuamba said the applicant for the order was his brother-in-law, a candidate of the ruling UDF party whom he had twice beaten in general elections.

Opposition parties MCP and Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) boycotted parliament in July this year in protest at President Bakili Muluzi appointing into his cabinet members from the opposition without their parties' approval.
The ruling UDF, with only 84 seats, resumed parliamentary proceedings last Monday without meeting the constitutional requirement of a quorum of the 177-seat parliament.
